headline: COPPER SHATTERS ALL-TIME HIGH AT $14,779 — TARIFF FEARS DRAIN U.S. STOCKPILES AS MINE SUPPLY CONTRACTS 1.1%; ANALYSTS CALL $15,000 THIS WEEK
snippet: LME copper hit an all-time high of $14,779 per metric tonne on September 8, 2026 — its third consecutive record-setting session and 17% above its 2025 year-end close — as markets priced in a dual shock: a proposed U.S. 15% tariff on refined copper imports (rising to 30% by 2028) is pulling physical metal into American warehouses, while first-half global mined copper output fell 1.1% and concentrate production dropped 2.6%, driven by ongoing disruptions at Codelco, Freeport-McMoRan, Antofagasta, and Ivanhoe. Analysts are now openly targeting a $15,000 test this week; for junior copper explorers on the TSX-V and ASX, a sustained move through $15,000 converts previously marginal resource estimates into project economics that attract institutional capital without requiring a merger event.

headline: RIO TINTO ACQUIRES AURUKUN BAUXITE FROM GLENCORE AND MITSUBISHI — CAPE YORK PROJECT 200KM FROM WEIPA SETS UP AUSTRALIA'S NEXT ALUMINIUM GIANT
snippet: Rio Tinto agreed on September 8, 2026 to acquire the Aurukun Bauxite Project in Cape York, Queensland, from Glencore (majority stake) and Mitsubishi Development (approximately 30%), with financial terms undisclosed, under the strategic rationale that Rio's Weipa operations — approximately 200 kilometres north — make it the natural owner to advance the project from its current Mineral Development Licence through a Mining Lease and into production. Both Glencore and Mitsubishi agreed that Rio's regional mine infrastructure gives Aurukun its best development path; completion remains subject to Queensland government and ACCC approvals, meaning the near-term market signal is less about production timelines and more about Rio's conviction that bauxite and aluminium demand from battery, construction, and advanced manufacturing end-markets justifies building out Australia's Cape York bauxite province further.

headline: GOLDGROUP HITS 16.8M AT 4.36 g/t AU AT SAN FRANCISCO — FIRST 6 HOLES OF 26,000M SONORA RESTART STUDY VALIDATE HIGH-GRADE OXIDE UPSIDE
snippet: Goldgroup Mining Inc. (TSX-V/NYSE American: GORO) released assay results on September 8, 2026 from the first six holes of its 26,000-metre drill program at the historically producing San Francisco Gold Project in Sonora, Mexico, led by hole GGD-178 with 16.8 metres at 4.36 g/t Au plus an adjacent 10.0 metres at 2.00 g/t Au, and GGD-174 returning 23.4 metres at 1.71 g/t Au; hole GGD-179 intersected 51.0 metres at 0.58 g/t Au including 3.9 metres at 2.53 g/t Au. Results are being incorporated into geological and resource models supporting an approximately US$8.5 million technical study evaluating a production restart at this open-pit oxide project — a mine that previously produced gold and sits in Sonora's established mining jurisdiction, where at today's $4,400+ gold price even a mid-grade oxide restart carries meaningful economics.

headline: GOLD ERASES 2026 GAINS AS FED HIKE BETS HIT 70% — SPOT AT $4,400, 19% BELOW JAN 28 RECORD; ELDORADO, AGNICO EAGLE EACH DOWN 3%+
snippet: Gold fell for a third consecutive session on September 8, 2026, erasing virtually all of its 2026 gains and trading near $4,400 — 19% below the January 28 record close of $5,419.83 and up a mere 0.7% year-to-date — as markets priced a roughly 70% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike at the September 16 meeting, driven by Friday's stronger-than-expected jobs report and a global bond selloff that pushed 10-year Treasury yields to multi-year highs. Gold equities tracked the metal lower: Eldorado Gold (-3.2%), Agnico Eagle (-2.8%), Equinox Gold (-2.7%), and Alamos Gold (-2.7%) all declined; Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI are the next binary catalysts, with the gold bull case resting on the view that any hike that triggers a growth slowdown will ultimately force an easing cycle that re-anchors the real rates underpinning the structural debasement trade.

headline: BHP AND KGHM SIGN GLOBAL COPPER EXPLORATION MOU — WORLD'S LARGEST MINER TEAMS WITH EU'S LEADING COPPER PRODUCER TO HUNT NEW DEPOSITS
snippet: BHP World Exploration and KGHM Polska Miedź signed a Memorandum of Understanding on September 8, 2026, establishing a framework for dialogue on joint copper exploration areas of interest globally — KGHM being the European Union's largest primary copper producer and the world's second-largest silver producer, with extensive underground mining expertise from the Legnica-Glogow Copper Belt in Poland. The MOU provides for knowledge sharing, operational practice comparison, and identification of potential joint exploration or development opportunities; while it is a framework rather than a funded commitment, the strategic pairing of BHP's global exploration reach with KGHM's state-influenced mandate to secure European copper supply signals an acceleration in the search for the next generation of undiscovered porphyry deposits at a moment when LME copper is setting all-time highs.

headline: KING COPPER ADVANCES 36,000M COLQUEMAYO DRILL CONTRACT — 59-HOLE PORPHYRY HUNT ACROSS 12KM × 4KM PERU SYSTEM MOVES TO FINAL CONTRACTOR SELECTION
snippet: King Copper Discovery Corp. announced on September 8, 2026 that it has completed site visits and technical reviews with drilling contractors bidding on its fully-funded, 36,000-metre, 40-platform, 59-hole diamond drill program at the Colquemayo Copper Project in Moquegua, southern Peru — the final step before contract execution and mobilization. The Colquemayo system spans approximately 12 kilometres by 4 kilometres with three priority copper-gold-molybdenum porphyry targets (Amata-Cairani, Coripuquio, Yanarico) defined through King Copper's geological reinterpretation of a system the company believes was historically under-tested at depth; at LME copper above $14,700 per tonne, first-hole results from a previously untested porphyry target in a proven Peruvian copper district carry meaningful re-rating potential for a junior with the permit, the funding, and the contractor nearly in place.

headline: GOLD STOCKS' AUTUMN RALLY: HAMILTON PROJECTS 10.1% AVERAGE SEASON; JUNIORS LEAD WHEN GOLD REBOUNDS FROM OVERSOLD CONDITIONS
snippet: Adam Hamilton at ZealLLC argues in a September 2026 GoldSeek column that gold stocks are entering their historically strongest seasonal period — the autumn rally that has averaged 10.1% gains for major gold miners over 25 years — from a technically oversold position relative to gold, with the metal sitting nearly $1,000 below its January 28 record and equities offering above-average leverage to any recovery. Hamilton's framework specifically favours mid-tier and junior gold miners over majors during gold uplegs, citing their higher operating leverage to gold price changes; major gold stocks already showed 3.7% month-to-date gains into the seasonal peak window before the September 8 selloff reset the entry point — creating what Hamilton's analysis characterises as a seasonal setup with unusually wide potential upside if gold's autumn rally this year compounds on a recovery from deeply oversold levels.

headline: RARE EARTH SEPTEMBER: GERMANIUM SURGES 10% AS NdPr BLOC FALLS TOGETHER — CHINA'S NOVEMBER 10 EXPORT CONTROL RESET IS THE ONLY CATALYST THAT MATTERS
snippet: The September 2026 rare earth market shows a near-flat basket (average +0.31%, median +0.22%) with a sharp internal divergence: germanium led gains at +10.04% as China's industrial technology export controls continue to bite Western semiconductor and infrared-optics supply chains, while the NdPr magnet complex — neodymium, praseodymium, and NdPr alloy — fell together as a block for the first time since May, a correlation event that typically signals short-term speculative unwinding rather than a fundamental demand shift in EV motor and wind turbine magnet materials. The single most important date for the sector remains November 10, 2026, when China's enhanced rare earth export control suspension resets; how Beijing frames the renewal — extension, expansion, or partial lifting — will set the sector's directional trade through Q4 and into 2027's anticipated supply gap from project delays in Australia, Canada, and Greenland.
